text_blocks.snippet: Yes, Illinois has mandatory vaccination requirements for students attending public and private schools. Students must show proof of immunization against several diseases to enroll in school. These requirements include vaccines for chickenpox, diphtheria, Hepatitis B, Hib, measles, meningitis, mumps, pertussis, polio, pneumococcal disease, rubella, and tetanus. There are also specific requirements for certain grades, such as Kindergarten, 6th, and 9th grades, regarding varicella (chickenpox) vaccines.
